newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Angus and Coote sees minimal year profit.
newsitem.headline: Angus and Coote sees minimal year profit.

text.p: Jewellery retailer Angus and Coote Ltd said on Wednesday it expected to post a "minimal" profit before abnormals and tax for the year to June 30, due to patchy and inconsistent trading in the second half.
The company also announced it has raised A$2.44 million through a placement of 10 percent of its share capital at A$2.60 a share to seven investors.
And directors had decided to make a one-for-20 bonus issue in lieu of a cash dividend, in view of the anticipated trading outcome, it said in a statement.
Angus and Coote said the forecast annual result reflected lower than normal sales, and continuing increases in fixed uncontrollable costs from rental increases in regional shopping centres.
"The forecast result for the year is particularly disappointing given the strong results achieved in the first half," the company said in a statement.
Angus and Coote more than doubled first-half profit before tax and abnormals from a year earlier to A$6.75 million, following the acquisition of Goldmark Jewellers & Edments stores.
The company said additional capital raised by the placement would be used to expand its capital base and reduce debt.
